## door v0.1.6 — the supervisor is fully sandboxed (Tier 4 Landlock)

This release completes door's **supervisor hardening milestone (M5)**. The
privileged daemon now runs under a **Landlock filesystem sandbox** in addition
to the Tier 3 seccomp syscall filter shipped in 0.1.4 — so a compromise of the
login daemon can no longer read `/home`, `/root`, `/var`, or `/tmp`, or write
outside the two runtime paths it actually needs. All four sandbox tiers
(pre-forked spawner + capability drop + seccomp + Landlock) now ship enabled by
default.

### Added
- **Tier 4 Landlock path sandbox** on the supervisor
  (`Environment=DOORD_LANDLOCK=enforce` in `doord.service`). The daemon confines
  **itself** to read/exec on `/usr /etc /proc /sys /run` and read/write on
  `/run/doord` and `/dev`, denying every other path — most sharply the user data
  under `/home` and `/root`. Applied supervisor-only, after the pre-forked
  spawner has moved session/greeter spawn off the daemon's lineage, so the
  ruleset **never confines your desktop session**.

### Security
- Landlock composes with the existing seccomp filter and capability drop as the
  **filesystem axis** of the supervisor sandbox. It bounds the blast radius of a
  bug in the IPC seam, PAM, or any linked dependency to the login role's minimal
  path set. Threat model:
  **[landlock-path-threat-model.md](https://github.com/satorisage/door/blob/master/.agent/SECURITY/landlock-path-threat-model.md)**.
- ABI pinned to Landlock V1 (path access, not device `ioctl` governance) so DRM
  master / VT control is never at risk. Best-effort: on a kernel without
  Landlock the daemon logs the real enforcement level rather than failing to
  start.

### Notes
- **Validated on real hardware.** A `DOORD_LANDLOCK=enforce` boot ran a full
  login → logout → greeter-recycle → re-login cycle clean with the shipped path
  seed — zero denials — before this flip. Landlock has no permissive/log mode,
  so the seed was tuned enumerate-then-enforce rather than from a log-only run.
- **Reversible.** Unset `DOORD_LANDLOCK` (or `=off`) drops the ruleset;
  `DOORD_NO_SANDBOX=1` forces the whole sandbox off for lockout recovery from a
  TTY. A too-tight seed surfaces as a recoverable `EACCES` login failure, never
  a wedged daemon.
